status: open dependency review; neither a normative erratum nor a completed obligation

normativeAnchors.name: checkStepSubperformanceSpecialization
expressions: owningType <> null and     (owningType.oclIsKindOf(Behavior) or      owningType.oclIsKindOf(Step)) and     self.isComposite implies     specializesFromLibrary('Performances::Performance::subperformance')

normativeAnchors.name: checkStepEnclosedPerformanceSpecialization
expressions: owningType <> null and     (owningType.oclIsKindOf(Behavior) or      owningType.oclIsKindOf(Step)) implies     specializesFromLibrary('Performances::Performance::enclosedPerformance')

normativeAnchors.name: checkStepOwnedPerformanceSpecialization
expressions: isComposite and owningType <> null and (owningType.oclIsKindOf(Structure) or  owningType.oclIsKindOf(Feature) and  owningType.oclAsType(Feature).type->     exists(oclIsKindOf(Structure)) implies     specializesFromLibrary('Objects::Object::ownedPerformance')

sourceConflict.ruleBoundary: KerML 1.0 8.3.4.6.3 and 8.4.4.7.2 use singular enclosedPerformance, subperformance and ownedPerformance names.
sourceConflict.libraryBoundary: The pinned Performances library and KerML 9.2.6.2.14 declare enclosedPerformances and subperformances. SysML action semantics also use the plural paths.

reportedIssue.title: Step OCL Issues
reportedIssue.finding: The OMG issue reports singular/plural target-name discrepancies for the enclosed and owned performance constraints. It is corroborating evidence, not an adopted resolution.

relatedSemanticsIssue.title: Steps are not always time enclosed
relatedSemanticsIssue.finding: A separate issue questions the temporal meaning of the Step specialization constraints; correcting a target spelling does not resolve that broader semantics issue.

sourceConflict.disposition: Keep this obligation open. Any use of the declared plural library identity needs an explicit interpretation record and positive/negative construction evidence; do not invent singular library members or claim an approved OMG correction.

probe.interpretation: Compatibility result selection locates the candidate result. The checked Type.feature report remains incomplete for the nested reference result and unsupported for the Boolean literal result owned by a Predicate. The compatibility specialization result is not itself a complete negative proof.

nextAcceptancePartitions: Certify Predicate and its return Features using required BooleanEvaluation heritage, inherited/owned result membership, complete positional redefinitions and missing-library/cycle/mutation counterexamples.
Audit nested reference and literal expression construction against Step enclosed-performance requirements. Resolve the recorded target-name discrepancy before complete source heritage is certified.
Provide checked expression-result selection for direct references, deferred when wrappers, literals and invocations; retain explicit unknown on missing/malformed/wrong-order result evidence.
Only then replace the three trigger validators using complete argument/result/wrapper and quantity-reference facts with canonical diagnostic names.
